passage:
“Why are you making that face?” said Tenzin. “You look like a fish.”
“I'm not.”
“You're sucking your cheeks in. Are you angry with me?”
Nirmala let her cheeks go. “No. I'm nervous about my dance recital tomorrow. I bite the inside of my cheek when I'm nervous. Don't stare.”
“Sorry.” Tenzin scratched his head. “Want to practise in front of me? I'll just watch. No comments on faces.”
Nirmala took a breath. “Okay. Just the first part.”

qa.q: What is Nirmala nervous about?
qa.a: She is nervous about her dance recital tomorrow.

qa.q: What was Nirmala feeling when she drew in her cheeks, and what did Tenzin first think it meant?
qa.a: She was nervous about the recital, and the cheek habit calms her. Tenzin first thought she was angry with him, since it looked like a grimace.

qa.q: What could Tenzin do to support Nirmala?
qa.a: Do what he offered: watch quietly, skip comments about her face and let her practise at her own pace.

qa.q: Why might Tenzin have misread Nirmala's face?
qa.a: Drawn-in cheeks look like a grimace or a scowl, and he could not see her worry. He asked instead of assuming, which helped.

grounding: Drawn-in cheeks and cheek biting are self-soothing from nerves, not ill will.

passage: I'm Nandini. I bite the inside of my cheek when I concentrate or get nervous. In class today Sunaina looked at me and asked, “Are you cross with someone?” I said, “No, I'm thinking.” Then I realised my face looks like a grimace when I do it. So I told her, “It's just a habit when I'm nervous about the test.” She said, “Oh, I do something too. I twist my hair.” We both laughed. I didn't feel so odd after that.

qa.q: What does Nandini do when she concentrates or gets nervous?
qa.a: She bites the inside of her cheek.

qa.q: What was Nandini feeling when Sunaina asked if she was cross, and what did Sunaina think?
qa.a: Nandini was nervous about the test and concentrating. Sunaina thought Nandini looked cross, because the cheek biting looks like a grimace.

qa.q: What worked when Nandini explained her habit?
qa.a: She said plainly that it is a habit when nervous, so Sunaina understood and shared her own habit of twisting her hair.

qa.q: How might Sunaina have felt when Nandini said she was only thinking?
qa.a: Probably relieved that Nandini was not upset with someone. She was also comfortable enough to admit her own habit.

grounding: Cheek biting from nerves looks like a grimace but is self-soothing.

passage: Music room note, Saturday. Vidya, harmonium teacher. During today's practice exam Gurleen sucked her cheeks in and chewed the inside of one the whole time she played. From the side it looked like a sour face. The visiting examiner wrote “seems unhappy to be here, attitude?” on her sheet. I've taught Gurleen for two years. She does this whenever a piece gets hard, and also when she's nervous, like today. It's how she steadies herself. I spoke to the examiner and had the comment removed. I told Gurleen her face is her own business, but if her cheek gets sore, we can try slow breaths instead.

qa.q: What did the visiting examiner write on Gurleen's sheet?
qa.a: The examiner wrote “seems unhappy to be here, attitude?” on her sheet.

qa.q: What was Gurleen most likely feeling as she chewed her cheek?
qa.a: She was most likely nervous about the exam and concentrating hard on a difficult piece, not unhappy or rude.

qa.q: Which of Vidya's steps helped Gurleen most?
qa.a: Having the unfair comment removed protected Gurleen, and offering slow breaths for a sore cheek respected the habit while giving another option.

qa.q: Why might the examiner read the face as attitude?
qa.a: Seeing Gurleen only once and from the side, the examiner took the sucked-in cheeks for a sour face, without knowing her habit.

grounding: Shows a child's cheek-chewing from nerves and concentration being misread as attitude, and a teacher explaining it is a self-soothing habit.

passage: Sunday night. It's Indu, writing in bed. Today Leela showed me her drawing of our street for the competition. I was also thinking about my own entry, which I haven't finished, and I was chewing the inside of my cheek like I always do when I'm worried. Leela's face fell. “You hate it. You made a face.” I didn't even know my face was doing anything! I told her about the cheek thing and said the windows in her drawing are better than mine. She said, “Then stop chewing, you look like you ate a lemon.” I laughed, but I'll probably still do it. It helps me think.

qa.q: What was Leela's drawing of?
qa.a: Leela's drawing was of their street, for the competition.

qa.q: What was Indu feeling while chewing the inside of the cheek?
qa.a: Indu felt worried about the unfinished entry, and the chewing was a self-soothing habit, not a comment on Leela's drawing.

qa.q: How did Indu fix the misunderstanding?
qa.a: Indu explained the cheek-chewing habit and gave real praise for the windows, which reassured Leela.

qa.q: How did Leela see Indu's face?
qa.a: Leela saw a face of dislike and felt hurt, until Indu explained it.

grounding: Shows a child's nervous cheek-chewing being mistaken for a grimace of dislike, when it is a self-soothing habit.

passage: Outside the kirana shop in their small town, Naveen was fixing the slipped chain on his cycle, cheeks sucked in so hard his face looked hollow. Simran walked past with her mother's shopping bag and waved. Naveen didn't wave back; his cheeks stayed pinched, his jaw working. Simran's smile dropped. Still angry about the kho-kho game, then. She almost walked on. Then she noticed his oily fingers, the chain half-hooked, and his tongue pressing inside one cheek. She waited. The chain clicked in. Naveen's face relaxed completely. “Oh, Simran! Hi! Did you see? I fixed it myself.”

qa.q: What was Naveen fixing?
qa.a: Naveen was fixing the slipped chain on his cycle.

qa.q: What was Simran feeling when Naveen didn't wave back?
qa.a: She felt hurt and uneasy, thinking he was still angry about the kho-kho game.

qa.q: What did Simran do that stopped a misunderstanding?
qa.a: She looked at the context, his oily fingers and the half-hooked chain, and waited instead of walking off.

qa.q: What was the moment like for Naveen?
qa.a: Naveen was so focused on the chain that he didn't notice Simran at first, and felt proud and happy once it clicked in.

grounding: Shows a child's drawn-in cheeks while concentrating looking like ill will, when it is a focus habit.

passage:
At the junior chess club in Dublin, Gabriel sat hunched over the board, cheeks sucked in, chewing the inside of one cheek. Across the table, Liam shifted in his chair. Every time Gabriel moved a knight, the face got tighter, as if he'd tasted something sour.

Liam put up his hand. "He's pulling faces at me. It's putting me off."

The club leader, Ms Byrne, crouched beside them. "Gabriel, are you doing that on purpose?"

Gabriel's cheeks popped out. He went pink. "Doing what? I always do that when I think. My mum says I'll chew a hole in my mouth."

Liam looked at the board, then at him, and almost laughed.

qa.q: What was Gabriel chewing while he thought?
qa.a: The inside of one cheek.

qa.q: Why did Liam put up his hand to complain?
qa.a: Liam felt uneasy and put off, reading Gabriel's tight, sour-looking face as a grimace aimed at him.

qa.q: What did Ms Byrne do that helped both boys?
qa.a: She asked Gabriel directly instead of scolding him, which showed the face was a thinking habit, not ill will.

qa.q: What is it like for Gabriel to learn his face was read as rude?
qa.a: Gabriel is surprised and embarrassed, since the cheek-chewing is just how he concentrates and calms himself.

grounding: It shows a child's drawn-in, chewed cheeks from concentration being misread as a grimace at an opponent, and a question clearing it up.
